messages:
alerts-bot: paging oncall - Latency SLO breach (p99 streaming) for customer MarinerHealth on us-west-2-dedicated-2. Alerts: p99 tail hitting 7.4s, normal ~0.9s. Incident ID: INC-2026-0479. Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-0479 :rotating_light:
maya: acked. i'm on it. pulling logs now.
rajesh: i'm available to help with routing/fallback toggles.
eli: i'm watching metrics - looks like a correlated spike across 3 pods in pool d2-gpu-a.
sre-jen: joining. any customer-facing impact?
maya: MarinerHealth reported UI stalls for admin actions using streaming chat. They use single-tenant dedicated pool d2-gpu-a, concurrency burst ~120 req/s at 18:42 UTC.
eli: metric snapshot (18:40-18:46):
```
pool=d2-gpu-a p95=320ms p99=7400ms streaming_success_rate=87% connection_retries=4x
per-pod: pod-12 cpu 78% gpu_util 92% stall_count 18
pod-14 cpu 81% gpu_util 95% stall_count 20
pod-16 cpu 65% gpu_util 91% stall_count 2
```
maya: interesting: stalls concentrated on pods handling long-prefix prompts (prefix starts with "PATIENT_SUMMARY:"). suspect KV cache thrash / long prefix causing repeated re-encodings.
rajesh: can you dump recent prompt length histogram?
maya: histogram: 0-512 tokens 48%, 512-2048 32%, 2048-8192 18%, >8192 2% (the >8192 are the PATIENT_SUMMARY requests).
eli: those long prefixes explain tail. also seeing increased kv cache miss rate and mem pressure on pod-14. possible OOM thrash leading to streaming stalls.
ops-bot: Pod pod-14 restarted by kube due to liveness probe timeout at 18:43:12 UTC.
sre-jen: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable model fallback to quantized variant on the pool, 2) route large-prefix sessions to a lower-concurrency lane, 3) temporarily increase dedicated pool capacity, 4) throttle per-session concurrency for MarinerHealth.
maya: executing 1 and 4 in parallel. eli please prepare routing rule.
eli: preparing a weighted routing rule. will route requests with prefix match "PATIENT_SUMMARY:" to fallback lane mariner-legacy (lower concurrency, more memory). applying rule now.
```
# routing rule (preview)
match: request.body.startswith("PATIENT_SUMMARY:")
route: pool=mariner-legacy,model=gpt-open-7b-q4,priority=high
```
rajesh: toggling model fallback on d2-gpu-a to gpt-open-7b-q4 for heavy requests. command: `rdctl pool update d2-gpu-a --fallback-model gpt-open-7b-q4`
maya: done. confirming rollout: control plane reports fallback active on 3/3 nodes.
eli: routing rule applied. starting to see traffic shift in 30s.
(1m later)
eli: metrics after changes (18:45-18:48): p99 down to 1.1s (from 7.4s), streaming_success_rate 98%. pod-12/pod-14 stall counts dropping.
sre-jen: nice. any customer-visible errors cleared?
maya: MarinerHealth confirmed UI responsive again. they saw partial restores at 18:46 UTC.
product-sam: what's root cause hypothesis? need a postmortem summary for customer.
rajesh: hypothesis: unusual workload mix from a scheduled batch of admin exports hit the dedicated pool with very long static prefixes (>>4k tokens). that caused repeated KV cache invalidations and memory pressure on a subset of pods (pod-14) -> liveness probe timeouts -> streaming stalls -> elevated p99.
maya: additional evidence: kube events show frequent snapshot GC on pod-14, and model memory footprint increased by 18% during the burst.
eli: also saw increased tokenization time due to unicode-heavy patient records. higher CPU on tokenizer thread.
sre-jen: mitigations to permanently reduce recurrence:
- Set a guardrail for per-request max prefix length per-tenant on dedicated pools
- Auto-route large-prefix sessions to a separate low-concurrency lane by default
- Improve KV cache eviction heuristics for long static prefixes
- Add early-reject+400 for >X tokens when a tenant hits concurrent long-prefix threshold

maya: creating follow-up ticket: RED-INC-0479-TKT in infra backlog. assigning to eng-runtime (rajesh/eli) and customer success for comms.
(roll call)
rajesh: i'll take infra tasks (routing + guardrail API).
eli: i'll own KV cache heuristic changes and telemetry improvements.
product-sam: i'll coordinate customer post-incident note and cs outreach.
sre-jen: i'll draft the incident timeline and verify SLAs.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0479 escalated to Severity 2 at 18:50 UTC.
maya: handing off to overnight oncall: @sre-jen will monitor for 2h, leave runbook notes.
sre-jen: noted. added runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/streaming-latency and timeline to the ticket.
maya: summary to include in runbook/incident channel: root cause hypothesis (long-prefix KV cache thrash + tokenizer overhead), immediate mitigations (model fallback to quantized variant + routing large prefixes to mariner-legacy lane + temporary throttle), customer impact (MarinerHealth UI stalls, ~14 minutes degradation window), next steps (guardrail, KV improvement, telemetry).
product-sam: customer update drafted and sent at 19:05 UTC.
eli: monitoring alerts reset to normal thresholds, no further p99 spikes in 40m window.
sre-jen: closing incident in channel. will keep ticket open for action items. feel free to ping if anything reappears. :white_check_mark:
